readings.title: The Plot Against Daniel
readings.subtitle: The governors conspire to create an unchangeable decree.
readings.text:
[Daniel 6:1] It pleased Dareyavesh to appoint over the reign one hundred and twenty viceroys, to be over all the reign,
[2] and over them three governors, of whom Dani’ěl was one, so that these viceroys should give account to them, and the sovereign suffer no loss.
[3] Then this Dani’ěl distinguished himself above the governors and viceroys, because an excellent spirit was in him. And the sovereign planned to appoint him over all the reign.
[4] Then the governors and viceroys sought to find <dn>את</dn> occasion against Dani’ěl concerning the reign. But they were unable to find occasion or corruption, because he was steadfast, and no negligence or corruption was found in him.
[5] Then these men said, “We shall not find <dn>את</dn> any occasion against this Dani’ěl unless we find it against him concerning the law of his <dn>Elah</dn>.”
[6] Then these governors and viceroys tumultuously gathered before the sovereign, and said this to him, “Sovereign Dareyavesh, live forever!
[7] “All the governors of the reign, the nobles and viceroys, the counsellors and advisors, have consulted together to establish a royal decree and to make a strong interdict, that whoever petitions any elah or man for thirty days, except you, O sovereign, is thrown into the den of lions.
[8] “Now, O sovereign, establish <dn>את</dn> the interdict and sign <dn>את</dn> the writing, so that it is not to be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which does not pass away.”
[9] So Sovereign Dareyavesh signed the written interdict.

readings.title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
readings.subtitle: Faithful in prayer, Daniel is cast into the den as the king laments.
readings.text:
[Daniel 6:10] And Dani’ěl, when he knew that the writing was signed, went home and in his upper room with his windows open toward Yerushalayim he knelt down on his knees three times a day, and prayed and gave thanks before his <dn>Elah</dn>, as he had done before.
[11] Then these men tumultuously gathered and found Dani’ěl praying and entreating before his <dn>Elah</dn>.
[12] Then they approached the sovereign, and spoke concerning the sovereign’s interdict, “Have you not signed a interdict that every man who petitions any elah or man within thirty days, except you, O sovereign, is thrown into the den of lions?” The sovereign answered and said, “The word is certain, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which does not pass away.”
[13] Then they answered and said before the sovereign, “Dani’ěl, who is one of the sons of the exile from Yehuḏah, pays no heed to you, O sovereign, nor for the interdict that you have signed, but makes his petition three times a day.”
[14] Then the sovereign, when he heard these words, was greatly displeased with himself, and set his heart on Dani’ěl to deliver him. And he laboured till the going down of the sun to deliver him.
[15] Then these men tumultuously gathered before the sovereign, and said to the sovereign, “Know, O sovereign, that it is the law of the Medes and Persians that any interdict or decree which the sovereign establishes is not to be changed.”
[16] Then the sovereign gave orders, and they brought Dani’ěl and threw him into the den of lions. But the sovereign spoke and said to Dani’ěl, “Your <dn>Elah</dn>, whom you serve continually, <dn>He</dn> Himself delivers you.”
[17] And a stone was brought and laid on the mouth of the den, and the sovereign sealed it with his own signet and with the signets of his great men, that the situation concerning Dani’ěl might not be changed.
[18] And the sovereign went to his palace and spent the night fasting. And no entertainment was brought before him, and his sleep fled from him.

readings.title: Deliverance and a New Decree
readings.subtitle: Daniel is found unharmed, his accusers are punished, and Darius honors the God of Daniel.
readings.text:
[Daniel 6:19] Then the sovereign rose up very early in the morning and hurried to the den of lions.
[20] And when he came to the den, he called with a grieved voice to Dani’ěl. The sovereign spoke and said to Dani’ěl, “Dani’ěl, servant of the living <dn>Elah</dn>, has your <dn>Elah</dn>, whom you serve continually, been able to deliver you from the lions?”
[21] Then Dani’ěl said to the sovereign, “O sovereign, live forever!
[22] “<dn>My</dn> <dn>Elah</dn> has sent <dn>His</dn> messenger and has shut the lions’ mouths, and they did not harm me, because <dn>I</dn> was found innocent before <dn>Him</dn>. And also before you, O sovereign, <dn>I</dn> have done no harm.”
[23] Then the sovereign was very glad and gave orders that Dani’ěl be taken up out of the den. And Dani’ěl was taken up out of the den, and no harm was found on him, because he trusted in his <dn>Elah</dn>.
[24] And the sovereign gave orders and they brought those men who had accused Dani’ěl, and they threw them, their children, and their wives into the den of lions. And the lions overpowered them, and broke all their bones in pieces before they reached the floor of the den.
[25] Then Sovereign Dareyavesh wrote to all peoples, nations, and languages that dwell in all the earth: “Peace be increased to you.
[26] “From before me is made a decree that throughout every rule of my reign men are to tremble and fear before the <dn>Elah</dn> of Dani’ěl, for <dn>He</dn> is the living <dn>Elah</dn>, and steadfast forever. And <dn>His</dn> reign is one which is not destroyed, and <dn>His</dn> rule is unto the end.
[27] “<dn>He</dn> delivers and rescues, and <dn>He</dn> works signs and wonders in the heavens and on earth, for <dn>He</dn> has delivered Dani’ěl from the power of the lions.”
[28] And this Dani’ěl prospered in the reign of Dareyavesh and in the reign of Koresh the Persian.

readings.title: Daniel's Prayer of Confession
readings.subtitle: Acknowledging Israel's sin, Daniel intercedes for the restoration of Jerusalem.
readings.text:
[Daniel 9:1] In the first year of Dareyavesh the son of Aḥashvěrosh, of the seed of the Medes, who was set up as sovereign over the reign of the Kasdim –
[2] in the first year of his reign <dn>I</dn>, Dani’ěl, observed from the Scriptures <dn>את</dn> the number of the years, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> given to Yirmeyah the prophet, for the completion of the wastes of Yerushalayim would be seventy years.
[3] So <dn>I</dn> set <dn>את</dn> <dn>my</dn> face toward <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> the <dn>Elohim</dn> to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes.
[4] And <dn>I</dn> prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, and made confession, and said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, great and awesome <dn>Ěl</dn>, guarding <dn>את</dn> the covenant and the loving-commitment to those who love <dn>Him</dn>, and to those who guard <dn>His</dn> commands.
[5] “We have sinned and did crookedness, and did wrong and rebelled, to turn aside from <dn>Your</dn> commands and from <dn>Your</dn> right-rulings.
[6] “And we have not listened to <dn>Your</dn> servants the prophets, who spoke in <dn>Your</dn> Name to our sovereigns, our heads, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.
[7] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to <dn>You</dn> is the righteousness, and to us the shame of face, as it is this day – to the men of Yehuḏah, to the inhabitants of Yerushalayim and all Yisra’ěl, those near and those far off in all the lands to which <dn>You</dn> have driven them, because of their trespass which they have trespassed against <dn>You</dn>.
[8] “O Master, to us is the shame of face, to our sovereigns, to our heads, and to our fathers, because we have sinned against <dn>You</dn>.
[9] “To <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> are the compassions and forgivenesses, for we have rebelled against <dn>Him</dn>.
[10] “And we have not obeyed the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, to walk in <dn>His</dn> Torot, which <dn>He</dn> set before us through <dn>His</dn> servants the prophets.
[11] “And all Yisra’ěl have transgressed <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> Torah, and turned aside, so as not to obey <dn>Your</dn> voice. So the curse and the oath written in the Torah of Mosheh the servant of <dn>Elohim</dn> have been poured out on us, for we have sinned against <dn>Him</dn>.
[12] “And <dn>He</dn> has confirmed <dn>His</dn> words, which <dn>He</dn> spoke against us and against our rulers who judged us, by bringing upon us great evil. For under all the heavens there has not been done like what was done to Yerushalayim.
[13] “As it is written in the Torah of Mosheh, all this evil has come upon us, and we have not entreated <dn>את</dn> the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, to turn back from our crookednesses, and to study <dn>Your</dn> truth.
[14] “Hence <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has watched over the evil and has brought it upon us. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> is righteous in all the works which <dn>He</dn> has done, but we have not obeyed <dn>His</dn> voice.
[15] “And now, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought <dn>Your</dn> people out of the land of Mitsrayim with a strong hand, and made <dn>Yourself</dn> a Name, as it is this day – we have sinned, we have done wrong!
[16] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, according to all <dn>Your</dn> righteousness, <dn>I</dn> pray, let <dn>Your</dn> displeasure and <dn>Your</dn> wrath be turned away from <dn>Your</dn> city Yerushalayim, <dn>Your</dn> set-apart mountain. For, because of our sins, and because of the crookednesses of our fathers, Yerushalayim and <dn>Your</dn> people have become a reproach to all those around us.
[17] “And now, our <dn>Elohim</dn>, hear the prayer of <dn>Your</dn> servant, and his supplications, and for the sake of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> cause <dn>Your</dn> face to shine on <dn>Your</dn> set-apart place, which is laid waste.
[18] “O <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, incline <dn>Your</dn> ear and hear. Open <dn>Your</dn> eyes and see our wastes, and the city which is called by <dn>Your</dn> Name. For we do not present our supplications before <dn>You</dn> because of our righteous deeds, but because of <dn>Your</dn> great compassions.
[19] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, hear! O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, forgive! O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, listen and act! Do not delay for <dn>Your</dn> own sake, <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, for <dn>Your</dn> city and <dn>Your</dn> people are called by <dn>Your</dn> Name.”

readings.title: The Prophecy of the Seventy Weeks
readings.subtitle: The messenger Gabriel reveals the timeline for redemption and the coming of the Messiah.
readings.text:
[Daniel 9:20] And while <dn>I</dn> was speaking, and praying, and confessing <dn>my</dn> sin and the sin of <dn>my</dn> people Yisra’ěl, and presenting <dn>my</dn> supplication before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> for the set-apart mountain of <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>,
[21] while <dn>I</dn> was still speaking in prayer, the man Gaḇri’ěl, whom <dn>I</dn> had seen in the vision at the beginning, came close to me, in swift flight about the time of the evening offering.
[22] And he made me understand, and talked with me, and said, “O Dani’ěl, <dn>I</dn> have now come forth to make you wise concerning understanding.
[23] “At the beginning of your supplications a word went out, and <dn>I</dn> have come to make it known, for you are greatly appreciated. So consider <dn>את</dn> the word and understand <dn>את</dn> the vision:
[24] “Seventy weeks are decreed for your people and for your set-apart city, to put an end to the transgression, and to seal up sins, and to cover crookedness, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up <dn>את</dn> vision and prophet, and to anoint the Most Set-apart.
[25] “Know, then, and understand: from the going forth of the command to restore and build Yerushalayim until Messiah the Prince is seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. It shall be built again, with streets and a trench, but in times of affliction.
[26] “And after the sixty-two weeks Messiah shall be cut off and have naught. And the people of a coming prince shall destroy the city and the set-apart place. And the end of it is with a flood. And wastes are decreed, and fighting until the end.
[27] “And he shall confirm a covenant with many for one week. And in the middle of the week he shall put an end to slaughtering and meal offering. And on the wing of abominations he shall lay waste, even until the complete end and that which is decreed is poured out on the one who lays waste.”

readings.title: The Proclamation of Liberation
readings.subtitle: Fulfilling prophecy, King Cyrus of Persia decrees the rebuilding of the Temple in Jerusalem.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 36:22] And in the first year of Koresh sovereign of Persia, in order to accomplish <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> by the mouth of Yirmeyahu, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stirred up the spirit of Koresh sovereign of Persia, so that he called out in all his reign, and also put it in writing, saying,
[23] “Thus said Koresh sovereign of Persia, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of the heavens has given me all the reigns of the earth. And <dn>He</dn> has commanded me to build <dn>Him</dn> a house in Yerushalayim, which is in Yehuḏah. Whoever is among you of all <dn>His</dn> people, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> be with him, and let him go up!’ ”
[Ezra 1:1] And in the first year of Koresh sovereign of Persia, that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> by the mouth of Yirmeyah might be accomplished, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stirred up <dn>את</dn> the spirit of Koresh sovereign of Persia, to proclaim throughout all his reign, and also in writing, saying,
[2] “Thus said Koresh sovereign of Persia, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of the heavens has given me all the reigns of the earth. And <dn>He</dn> has commanded me to build <dn>Him</dn> a house in Yerushalayim which is in Yehuḏah.
[3] Who is among you of all <dn>His</dn> people? <dn>His</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> be with him! And let him go up to Yerushalayim, which is in Yehuḏah, and build <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl – <dn>He</dn> is <dn>Elohim</dn> – which is in Yerushalayim.
[4] And whoever is left from all the places where he sojourns, let the men of his place help him with silver and gold, with goods and livestock, besides the voluntary offerings for the House of <dn>Elohim</dn> which is in Yerushalayim.’ ”

readings.title: The People Respond
readings.subtitle: The leaders of Judah and Benjamin prepare to return, equipped with provisions and the Temple's treasures.
readings.text:
[Ezra 1:5] And the heads of the fathers’ houses of Yehuḏah and Binyamin, and the priests and the Lěvites, with all those whose spirits <dn>Elohim</dn> had stirred, rose up to go up and build the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which is in Yerushalayim.
[6] And all those round about them strengthened their hands with objects of silver and gold, with goods and livestock, and with valuables, besides all that was voluntarily offered.
[7] And Sovereign Koresh brought out <dn>את</dn> the utensils of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar had taken from Yerushalayim and put in the house of his mighty ones,
[8] and Koresh sovereign of Persia brought them out by the hand of Mithreḏath the treasurer, and counted them out to Shěshbatstsar the leader of Yehuḏah.
[9] And this was their number: thirty gold dishes, one thousand silver dishes, twenty-nine knives,
[10] thirty gold basins, next, four hundred and ten silver basins, one thousand other utensils.
[11] All the utensils of gold and silver were five thousand four hundred. Shěshbatstsar took all of them with the exiles who were brought from Baḇel to Yerushalayim.

readings.title: The Descendants of Jeconiah
readings.subtitle: The line of the captive king, including Shealtiel and Zerubbabel.
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 3:17] And the sons of Yeḵonyah the captive: She’alti’ěl his son,
[18] and Malkiram, and Peḏayah, and Shenatstsar, Yeqamyah, Hoshama, and Neḏaḇyah.
[19] And the sons of Peḏayah: Zerubbaḇel and Shim‛i. The sons of Zerubbaḇel: Meshullam, and Ḥananyah, and Shelomith their sister,
